neighbours.label: the start of a sentence-opening reason clause (Because ..., Since ...), up to its subject and verb
fire: The soil here is thin and dry. Because of this, few crops grow.
The tax was unpopular with farmers. Because they rely on cheap fuel, it hurt.
The trail is often closed in winter. Since this route has few signs, go slowly.
Nurses are in short supply this year. Because training takes time, it will last.
The river floods nearly every spring. Because the town is low, it often suffers.
The law is hard to enforce. Since these rules have many gaps, firms ignore them.
Bees are vital to farming. Because they pollinate crops, their decline matters.
Prices rose again this quarter. Because demand is strong, sellers raised them.
quiet: The soil here is thin and dry, and few crops grow because of this.
The tax was unpopular with farmers, who rely on cheap fuel, and it hurt.
The trail is often closed in winter, and this route has few signs.
Nurses are in short supply this year, and the training takes time.
The river floods nearly every spring, and the town is low.
The law is hard to enforce, and these rules have many gaps.
Bees are vital to farming, and they pollinate crops every summer.
Prices rose again this quarter, and demand is strong in the region.

notes: Card: ' Because' x8, ' Since' x5, ' theory' x2, ' has' x2, ' they' x2, ' it' x2. Probes: 'Since this lesson has' 0.386, 'Because they' 0.354, 'Because' as the first word 0.311; 'because it rained' mid-sentence 0.016, plain sentence 0.002. Fire items follow an earlier sentence, as in the card. Near misses have mid-sentence 'because' or no reason clause.
